paper_metadata.title: LLaVA-Med: Training a Large Language-and-Vision Assistant for Biomedicine in One Day
paper_metadata.abstract: Conversational generative AI has demonstrated remarkable promise for empowering biomedical practitioners, but current investigations focus on unimodal text. Multimodal conversational AI has seen rapid progress by leveraging billions of image-text pairs from the public web, but such general-domain vision-language models still lack sophistication in understanding and conversing about biomedical images. In this paper, we propose a cost-efficient approach for training a vision-language conversational assistant that can answer open-ended research questions of biomedical images. The key idea is to leverage a large-scale, broad-coverage biomedical figure-caption dataset extracted from PubMed Central, use GPT-4 to self-instruct open-ended instruction-following data from the captions, and then fine-tune a large general-domain vision-language model using a novel curriculum learning method. Specifically, the model first learns to align biomedical vocabulary using the figure-caption pairs as is, then learns to master open-ended conversational semantics using GPT-4 generated instruction-following data, broadly mimicking how a layperson gradually acquires biomedical knowledge. This enables us to train a Large Language and Vision Assistant for BioMedicine (LLaVA-Med) in less than 15 hours (with eight A100s). LLaVA-Med exhibits excellent multimodal conversational capability and can follow open-ended instruction to assist with inquiries about a biomedical image. On three standard biomedical visual question answering datasets, LLaVA-Med outperforms previous supervised state-of-the-art on certain metrics. To facilitate biomedical multimodal research, we will release our instruction-following data and the LLaVA-Med model.

extraction_data.innovation: Two-stage curriculum learning for biomedical domain adaptation: (1) Biomedical Concept Feature Alignment filters PMC-15M to 600K pairs, freezing vision encoder and LM to update only a linear projection matrix for concept coverage; (2) Medical Instruction Tuning uses 60K GPT-4-generated instruction-following pairs (incorporating in-line figure mentions as external context) to enable conversational medical VQA, achieving domain adaptation in one day.
extraction_data.pretraining_corpus: PMC-15M (filtered to 600K for Stage 1), 60K biomedical instruction-following pairs (Stage 2)
extraction_data.finetuning_task: Biomedical visual instruction tuning, Medical visual instruction following, medical VQA, Biomedical visual question answering, instruction tuning
extraction_data.extension: Two-stage training pipeline: Stage 1 aligns vision encoder with biomedical text; Stage 2 fine-tunes on curated biomedical instruction data (10K/60K samples), followed by downstream fine-tuning.
extraction_data.research_problem: Biomedical visual question answering and open-ended instruction following for biomedical images.
extraction_data.application: Biomedical visual question answering, open-ended instruction following for biomedical images, conversational AI for biomedical practitioners.
extraction_data.paper_title: LLaVA-Med: Training a Large Language-and-Vision Assistant for Biomedicine in One Day
extraction_data.finetuning_data: GPT-4 generated instruction-following data from PMC-15M captions, PMC-15M (filtered), GPT-4-generated biomedical instruction-following data, VQA-RAD, PathVQA, SLAKE, 10K/60K biomedical instruction data, 60K-IM
extraction_data.training_pipeline: Two-stage curriculum learning: (1) align biomedical vocabulary using raw image-text pairs; (2) learn open-ended conversational semantics using GPT-4-generated instruction-following data.
extraction_data.synthetic_data_generation_method: GPT-4 generation of instruction-following data from figure captions and in-line figure mentions
extraction_data.fusion_architecture: MLP projector aligning visual features to language space
extraction_data.vision_encoder: BioMedCLIP / CLIP ViT-L/14, Vision encoder (specific backbone not named in text), BioMedCLIP, CLIP
